findings.summary: The prefix goes into a LIKE pattern unescaped, so _ and % in it match other databases' tables, which are then read and dropped.
A write that fails part way still commits, so tables already dropped or emptied stay that way.
Documents are read back ordered by their id as text, so ids 10 and 11 come before 2 instead of insertion order.
readonly=True opens the file with mode=rw, so a read-only storage can still change the file.

An empty prefix is accepted, so the LIKE pattern becomes %, every table in the file counts as one of this database's tables, and the next write drops the tables of every other database sharing the file.
